classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied triangle to identify the wall height as opposite the given angle and the ladder as hypotenuse, apply sine once, and express metres to the nearest centimetre.

content.prompt: A $5\text{ m}$ ladder leans against a wall, making an angle of $50^\circ$ with the floor. How far up the wall (correct to the nearest centimetre) is the top of the ladder?

spec.description: Unshaded right triangle with the ladder rising from bottom left to top right, a 5 m label on the ladder, a 50-degree floor angle and a right-angle marker at the wall base. Floor and wall extend slightly beyond the ladder endpoints. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The ladder is the hypotenuse. The required vertical height is opposite the 50-degree angle.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels remain visible; the unknown height and its value are absent.

answer.worked:
Let the height up the wall be $h$ metres. The height is opposite the angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse, so use sine.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{h}{5}&=\sin 50^\circ\\h&=5\sin 50^\circ\\h&\approx3.83\text{ m}\end{align*}$$

The top of the ladder is $3.83\text{ m}$ up the wall, correct to the nearest centimetre.
